name: english-connected-speech
note: Connected-speech processes of English, applied in this order to each sung line after note durations are known. Each rule names its family, a source, its effect, a gate and worked examples (phones with stress digits; '.' separates syllables, '#' words, '|' a phrase break (punctuation) that no rule crosses; d=<s> sets every syllable's duration). The examples are the rule's tests. Accent-specific processes belong in the accent file, not here. A gate of max_syl_d means the rule only fires on syllables shorter than that (slow singing keeps the full form).

sources.C14: Cruttenden, A. (2014) Gimson's Pronunciation of English, 8th ed., ch. 12 (connected speech: elision, assimilation, linking, weak forms)
sources.R09: Roach, P. (2009) English Phonetics and Phonology, 4th ed., ch. 12 and 14
sources.W82: Wells, J. C. (1982) Accents of English, vol. 1, 3.4
sources.L89: Labov, W. (1989) The child as linguistic historian, Language Variation and Change 1 (t/d deletion)

rules.does: an unstressed monosyllabic function word on a short note takes its weak form

examples.in: AE0 N D # D AW1 N
examples.out: AH0 N D # D AW1 N

examples.in: AE0 N D # D AW1 N
examples.out: AE0 N D # D AW1 N

rules.does: a word-final T or D that closes a voicing-matched consonant cluster drops before a consonant-initial word (not Y, which coalesces instead)

examples.in: AE0 N D # D AW1 N
M AH0 S T # G OH1
AE0 N D # AY1
W EH1 N T # D AW1 N
examples.out: W EH1 N T # D AW1 N

rules.does: two identical consonants across a word boundary are made as one, longer consonant

examples.in: B IH1 G # G ER1 L
DH IH1 S # S AO1 NG

rules.does: a word-final alveolar T, D or N takes the place of a following word-initial labial or velar

examples.in: T EH1 N # B OY1 Z
examples.out: T EH1 M # B OY1 Z

examples.in: G UH1 D # G ER1 L
examples.out: G UH1 G # G ER1 L

examples.in: T EH1 N # B OY1 Z
examples.out: T EH1 N # B OY1 Z

rules.does: a word-final T, D, S or Z and a following word-initial Y merge into CH, JH, SH or ZH

examples.in: D IH1 D # Y UW0
M IH1 S # Y UW0

rules.does: an unstressed IH or AH between a homorganic consonant (T, D, S, Z) and N or L is lost and the sonorant carries the syllable

examples.in: M AW1 N . T IH0 N
L IH1 . T AH0 L
M AW1 N . T IH0 N
examples.out: M AW1 N . T IH0 N

rules.does: between a word-final vowel and a word-initial vowel a short Y (after a front close end) or W (after a back rounded end) links them, instead of a glottal break

examples.in: S IY1 # IH0 T
G OH1 # AH0 . W EY1
examples.out: G OH1 # W: AH0 . W EY1

examples.in: DH AH0 # EH1 N D
B OY1 | OH1
